extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities, and researchers tracking DHS Federal Register notices (public commenters, agency compliance staff, OMB reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: A machine-readable listing of Department of Homeland Security Federal Register documents (rules, notices, certificates, etc.) including titles, abstracts, agencies, publication dates, and URLs; useful for locating notices that invite public comment or announce regulatory actions. The page aggregates multiple DHS subagency entries and abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) comment topics
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing an information collection notice, the agency invites the public and other Federal agencies to comment regarding the nature of the information collection, the categories of respondents, the estimated burden (i.e., the time, effort, and resources used by the respondents to respond), the estimated cost to the respondent, and the actual information collection instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies publish Information Collection Requests (ICRs) in the Federal Register to obtain public comment on these specific topics and then submit ICRs to OMB for review and approval in accordance with the PRA. Comments should address the listed topics (nature, respondent categories, burden, cost, instruments) and may be used to justify extension, reinstatement, or revision of collections. (This language recurs across multiple DHS ICR notices in the listing.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency submission of ICR to OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department (via a DHS component such as CBP or USCIS) will be submitting the following information collection request to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA). The information collection is published in the Federal Register to obtain comments from the public and affected agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices announcing submission to OMB should state the ICR being submitted, the PRA basis, and explicitly invite comments from both the general public and affected agencies. This is the procedural notice form agencies use when seeking OMB action (extension, reinstatement, or new collection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a temporary security/safety zone rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A temporary security/safety zone: establishes the regulated area (navigable waters, described spatially, e.g., between mile markers or in vicinity of a pier), states the purpose (e.g., provide waterside security and protection of persons under Secret Service protection; protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from hazards associated with construction activities, fireworks, or air shows), specifies the enforcement period (dates and times), and prescribes that entry into, transiting, anchoring in, or remaining in the zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port or a designated on-scene U.S. Coast Guard representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule text should give precise geographic boundaries (mile markers, piers, named waterways), a clear articulation of the safety/security need motivating the temporary zone, exact enforcement start/end (dates/times), and a statement of prohibited conduct with exceptions that authorize the Captain of the Port or designated representative to permit entry. This pattern appears in multiple Coast Guard rule abstracts (security zones, safety zones, fireworks, festival security).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special local regulations for marine events—required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending a special local regulation for marine events, the agency adds or specifies enforcement periods during which the regulation is subject to enforcement and states the action is necessary to provide for the safety of life on navigable waters during the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should identify the regulated area, the event (e.g., Fleet Week), the specific enforcement windows (weeks/dates), and state prohibitions (persons/vessels may not enter the regulated area during enforcement unless authorized by the Captain of the Port or Coast Guard Patrol Commander).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Alternative Compliance notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice announcing issuance of a certificate of alternative compliance must identify the vessel, state that the issuing Coast Guard district has issued a certificate of alternative compliance from the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972 (72 COLREGS), and explain why the vessel cannot fully comply with certain COLREGS provisions (for example, construction and placement of superstructure and working deck prevent compliance with lighting provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice should cite the statutory requirement to publish the certificate, explain the specific design-related inability to comply with COLREGS provisions, and articulate that issuance promotes the Coast Guard's marine safety mission. Include vessel identifying information (name, ON number) and the nature of the relief granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation and approval notices (commercial gauger and laboratory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices pursuant to CBP regulations must state that an entity has been approved/accredited to gauge and/or test specified commodities (e.g., petroleum and certain petroleum products) for customs purposes, identify the entity (name and location), and specify the approval/accreditation term (for example, three years as of a stated effective date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such notices should cite the regulatory authority, list the scope of accreditation (what products and what activities—gauging, testing), provide the effective/expiration dates, and indicate any statutory or regulatory citations that govern the approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction/clarification notices for prior Federal Register entries
rubrics_metrics.description: When an earlier Federal Register notice contained incorrect statements (e.g., misstated applicability dates or thresholds), a subsequent notice should correct the record and state the correct applicability (for example, whether updated thresholds apply to major disasters declared by the President on or after a specified date, rather than incident start dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction notices must identify the earlier notice (date and citation), specify the error, provide the corrected text/interpretation, and clarify the effective/applicability date or scope. This ensures legal clarity for affected programs (e.g., FEMA public assistance thresholds).
